question: Does Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 outperform Top 50?
summary: As of the latest Official League snapshot, Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 (Hyperliquid / USDC, dynamic MarketCapPairList, Official feed, ~1 month live) definitively outperforms Top 50 (Bitget / USDT, static 50-pair whitelist, Restarted feed, launched today). Top 20 holds league rank #3 with a net total PnL of +7.89 across 63 closed trades (+62.50 USDC realized, 100% win rate, 1.77% average ROI). Top 50 is at rank #4 with a net total PnL of -28.44 across only 9 closed trades (+6.63 USDT realized, 100% win rate, 1.35% average ROI). Top 20’s unrealized drawdown is roughly 0.9× its realized profit buffer, whereas Top 50’s is roughly 5.3× realized gains, leaving the latter structurally more vulnerable to carry-risk. Per-trade ROI, initially unstable and nominally higher for Top 50 with tiny samples, has declined to 1.35% as more trades closed, now trailing Top 20’s 1.77%. Severe confounders—different exchanges, margin currencies, dynamic vs static pairlists, and Official vs Restarted data quality—prevent an apples-to-apples strategy comparison. The operator also notes the broader Cosmo/Wanda ecosystem has ~2 years of positive live history, mostly with ~20 pairs. Conclusion: Top 20 is the clear aggregate outperformer on realized profit, throughput, total PnL, and power ranking. Reassessment is warranted once Top 50 exceeds 20 closed trades and achieves gapless Official feed continuity on a comparable exchange/currency baseline.

Live-site and indexed trajectories show a persistent performance chasm: Top 20 (Hyperliquid/USDC, Official feed, dynamic MarketCapPairList) holds a net total PnL near +10 with 64 closed trades, +62.84 USDC realized, stable ~1.75% average ROI, and a balanced unrealized-to-realized ratio (~0.84×). The composite power-ranking gap is unchanged at roughly 120 vs 54. Repo excerpts and local research identify a persistent non-exchange confounder: Top 20 uses a dynamic MarketCapPairList (number_assets: 20, refresh_period: 86400) rotating into the highest-market-cap pairs, while Top 50 relies on a static 50-pair whitelist. Local notes state this dynamic concentration delivers superior liquidity alignment and actionable exits, whereas the static whitelist accumulates adverse carry in lower-tier pairs. Operator history (~2 years of positive live track record with ~20 pairs) further supports the narrower dynamic universe as the proven configuration. Strictly from local evidence, the conclusion is that Top 50 is unlikely to close the PnL or power-ranking gap solely by crossing the 20-trade threshold on comparable exchange/currency infrastructure; the 20-pair dynamic universe retains a structural edge in per-trade efficiency, signal conversion, and risk-buffer balance.
